newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Hungary receives warm welcome at NATO.
newsitem.headline: Hungary receives warm welcome at NATO.

text.p: Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said on Wednesday he had received the clearest indication yet his country would be among those invited to join NATO later this year.
"All ambassadors said they supported Hungary's application," Kovacs told reporters after meeting the 16 alliance ambassadors permanently based at NATO's Brussels headquarters.
Hungary, along with the Czech Republic and Poland, is expected to be invited to join the alliance at a special summit in Madrid next July.

Kovac was in Brussels to brief NATO on his country's preparations to join the alliance. The alliance is giving all candidate countries the chance to push their case one last time before a final decision is taken in a few weeks time.

NATO officials said Hungary had made great progress in restructuring its armed forces since the country shed its communist past and in settling outstanding border disputes with its neighbours -- two key conditions of membership.
Diplomats stressed no official decision had yet been taken but said Budapest had been treated as if it was "almost in".
"No-one explicitly told Kovacs, Hungary is in but there is a sort of implicit recognition it will be invited to join. Hungary and Kovacs are well-known and popular at NATO hq," said one diplomat.

Hungary has won many friends among NATO countries for its participation in the alliance-led peacekeeping efforts in Bosnia and for making its territory and facilities available for the huge support operation.
